clue.text: Carbon or nitrogen as the result of pressure?

parts.note: c is the chemical symbol for carbon
the little joining word is taken at face value and hands over its own two letters
n is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: A chemistry-lesson question about which element you get by squeezing something hard enough.
explanation.walkthrough: Squeeze carbon hard and you get a diamond, which is the answer the surface is offering; the real pressure here is a tight shoe on a toe.
explanation.definitionFit: A corn is the hard patch a tight shoe raises by pressing on one spot, so it is literally what pressure produces.

clue.text: Unbecoming in most of battle: a sharp punch

indicators.note: most of means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a fray is a battle or brawl
the last letter of fray, the one dropped
a dig is a sharp poke or jab

explanation.surface: Throwing a quick jab in the thick of a fight is not the done thing.
explanation.walkthrough: IN, then 'most of' FRAY, which is FRA, then DIG. The answer is from the Latin infra dignitatem, beneath one's dignity.
explanation.definitionFit: Infra dig, short for the Latin for 'beneath one's dignity', describes behaviour unbefitting someone's position.

clue.text: Nutritious fruit mostly very good? Excellent

indicators.note: mostly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: ace is slang for very good
the last letter of ace, the one dropped
A1 means excellent, with the figure 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A health-food fruit is said to be largely very good for you, and then excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' cuts ACE to AC, and A1, first-rate, is written AI with the 1 standing in for I.
explanation.definitionFit: Acai berries come from a South American palm and are marketed as a health food rich in antioxidants.

clue.text: New head of company is human so far

indicators.note: new here means freshly made over, so the letters take a fresh arrangement
the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the word whose first letter is used
the letters rearranged
the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: The new company chief is a mere human so far.
explanation.walkthrough: C, the 'head of' company, joins IS and HUMAN, and 'New' rearranges all eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Inasmuch, as in 'inasmuch as', means to the extent that, which is what 'so far as' also expresses.

clue.text: Children's writer reduced home a small amount

indicators.note: reduced means cut down by its last letter

parts.note: a nest is a home, especially a bird's
the last letter of nest, the one dropped
a bit is a small amount

explanation.surface: An author of children's books has downsized their house a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reduced' trims NEST to NES, followed by BIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith Nesbit wrote The Railway Children and Five Children and It, classic Edwardian novels for young readers.

clue.text: Tedium of the French lines on Spanish city, ignoring a mention of Spain

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: du is French for of the
L is the abbreviation for line, so LL is lines

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out one appearance of the letter for Spain

parts.note: Seville is a city in Andalusia
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A French writer's lines on Seville skip over Spain and prove tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a mention' signals removing just one of the two Es in SEVILLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dullsville is a slang name for a boring place or situation, so it stands for tedium.

clue.text: Takes careful steps in board game, losing last piece

indicators.note: losing its last piece means the word drops its final letter

parts.note: chess is a board game
the last letter of chess, the one dropped

explanation.surface: A chess player moves cautiously during a game, having lost a final piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing last piece' sounds like chess, which it is, but it cuts CHESS to CHES after IN.
explanation.definitionFit: To inch forward is to move slowly and carefully, a small distance at a time.

clue.text: Trivial hackneyed stuff after spicy stuff

indicators.note: coming after something in a down entry means being written below it, so this piece is second

parts.note: pepper is the spicy stuff, and it is named last but entered first
corn is hackneyed material, which is where corny comes from

explanation.surface: A comedian's stale material following the racy part of the act.
explanation.walkthrough: The adjective comes from British leases: a peppercorn rent is a token payment of one peppercorn a year, so peppercorn means nominal, not worth counting.
explanation.definitionFit: A peppercorn rent is a nominal one, and that legal use gives PEPPERCORN the adjective sense 'trivial'.

clue.text: Irrelevant old female never against series

parts.note: o = old, the standard abbreviation
f = female, as on a form
never is the flat refusal, no
con is against, as in the pros and cons
a sequence is a series of things in order

explanation.surface: An elderly woman who was never opposed to the series.
explanation.walkthrough: Five separate pieces stack up here, and the first two are single letters, which is what makes a fifteen-letter answer buildable at all. CON for against comes from the pros and cons.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of no consequence has no bearing on the matter in hand, which is exactly what calling it irrelevant says.

clue.text: Marine worms, source of each one collected by 26s

indicators.note: collected by means held inside the word that 26s gives

parts.note: the answer to 26 in this puzzle, in the plural: nerds

indicators.note: source of means the first letter of each

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Geeks gather marine worms, one of each, from the source.
explanation.definitionFit: Nereids are a family of bristle worms living in the sea, such as ragworms.

clue.text: Hotel worker with a lot of guts taking on hotel work

indicators.note: taking on means adding the next pieces after it
a lot of means most of the word for guts, dropping its last letter

parts.note: belly means the guts, stomach
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A hotel worker with plenty of guts takes on hotel duties.
explanation.definitionFit: A bellhop carries luggage and runs errands for guests in a hotel.

clue.text: Rioting led unrest in the final analysis

indicators.note: a riot is disorder in the street, and letters in disorder will not stay in the order they were handed to you

parts.note: anagram fodder, nine letters

explanation.surface: Looking back, it was the rioting that stirred up all the unrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rioting' reads as the subject of a sentence about civil disorder, which is the whole disguise: it is the instruction, and 'led unrest' is the nine letters to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: The final analysis and the END RESULT both name what a process comes down to once everything has been weighed up.

clue.text: Nonsense that is involved in change, sapping power and enthusiasm

indicators.note: involved in means set inside the shortened word for change
sapping means draining away, so the letter for power is taken out

parts.note: pence are small change
P is the physics symbol for power
bull is short for nonsense, as in bull and baloney
ie is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Nonsense gets into a change of plan, draining power and enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebullience is bubbling cheerfulness and energy, so it is high-spirited enthusiasm.

clue.text: Last blokes to accept attention and bit of touching affectionate banter

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the other word goes inside

parts.note: the end is the last part
men are blokes
to give an ear is to pay attention

indicators.note: a bit of a word here is its first letter

parts.note: the word whose first letter is used

explanation.surface: The final men to hear and be touched by some loving chat.
explanation.walkthrough: END and MEN 'accept' EAR between them, and a 'bit of' touching, T, ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: An endearment is a term of affection such as darling or sweetheart, the stuff of loving banter.

clue.text: Vanadium is used before gold for part of armour

indicators.note: being used before something puts this piece in front of the one that follows

parts.note: v is the chemical symbol for vanadium
the verb is taken at face value for its own letters
or is gold in heraldry, from the French

explanation.surface: A metallurgist's recipe in which one metal goes on before the gold.
explanation.walkthrough: Two conventions in five letters: V for vanadium off the periodic table, and OR for gold, which is the heraldic tincture and the French word.
explanation.definitionFit: A visor is the hinged face-guard of a helmet, so 'part of armour' names it by the suit it belongs to.

clue.text: Encouraged, clarified removing President

indicators.note: removing a letter takes it out of the word and closes the gap behind it

parts.note: purged means cleansed of what muddied it, which is one sense of clarified
p = President, and it is the letter taken out

explanation.surface: A speech tidied up by cutting the President out of it altogether.
explanation.walkthrough: 'President' sends most solvers hunting for IKE, ABE or a whole surname, and it is the single letter P. Clarified is the kitchen sense, as of butter or stock.
explanation.definitionFit: To urge somebody on is to encourage them, and both words are sitting in the past tense.

clue.text: About to be dismissed by group of women, being a poor performer

indicators.note: letters dismissed by a word are sent out of it, leaving what remains

parts.note: a harem is a household's group of women
re = about, as at the head of a memo, and these are the letters dismissed

explanation.surface: Somebody about to be sacked by a panel of women for a bad performance.
explanation.walkthrough: A ham is an actor who overplays every line, from the old ham-fatter of the music hall. 'About' looks like the point he is on the edge of and is two letters of the harem.
explanation.definitionFit: A ham is an actor who overacts, so 'a poor performer' is the theatrical sense of the word.

clue.text: Idiot turned up? Refuse to receive one contribution to thinking, perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: dim means stupid, idiotic

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: bran is the husks left over from grain, refuse
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A fool showed up? Say no to letting one person add to the brainstorm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Idiot' is DIM, here taken as a noun, which 'turned up' gives MID; BRAN 'receives' I.
explanation.definitionFit: The midbrain is the part of the brain between the forebrain and hindbrain, which plays a part in thinking.

clue.text: Release bricks (about ton)

indicators.note: something placed about another thing is wrapped around it

parts.note: Lego is the plastic brick every child has trodden on
t = ton, the standard abbreviation, and it goes inside

explanation.surface: Dropping a load of bricks that weigh about a ton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About ton' reads as roughly a ton, which is the trap; it is an instruction to wrap the bricks round a T. The bracket makes it look like an aside rather than the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To let go of something is to stop gripping it, which is the phrasal verb answering the plain one.

clue.text: Election concerns? Recommends including ballot box

indicators.note: whatever a word includes is written inside it

parts.note: to tout something is to recommend it loudly
an urn is the vessel votes are dropped into, and it goes inside

explanation.surface: Advice on running a polling station that says to include a ballot box.
explanation.walkthrough: A turnout is the share of voters who actually show up, the figure every party frets over on polling night; the question mark admits the definition is a loose way of saying so.
explanation.definitionFit: Turnouts are how many voters actually come out, which is what campaigns worry about most on election day.

clue.text: Asian city keeps invading American city

indicators.note: an invader goes inside the place it invades

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles, split open to take something in
to keep something is to have it

explanation.surface: One city permanently encroaching on another one across the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeps invading' reads as one phrase about repeated attacks, and the two words are doing different jobs: 'keeps' is the piece and 'invading' is the instruction. The city is the Tibetan capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Lhasa is the capital of Tibet, so 'Asian city' defines it as one instance of the class.

clue.text: Japanese plant university introduced to a Caribbean island

indicators.note: introducing one thing to another slides it in among the letters already there

parts.note: the clue's own a, then Cuba, the largest of the Caribbean islands
u = university, as in a place at one

explanation.surface: A university opening a campus on a Caribbean island.
explanation.walkthrough: The aucuba, or spotted laurel, is the glossy yellow-flecked shrub in half the front gardens in Britain, and it came originally from Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: The aucuba is a shrub native to Japan, so 'Japanese plant' defines it by where it comes from.

clue.text: Fluid gender, we start to suspect, in marsh bird

indicators.note: a fluid has no fixed shape, and letters with no fixed shape will not hold the order they are given in

parts.note: anagram fodder, eight letters

indicators.note: the start of the word that follows is the letter it begins with

parts.note: the first letter of 'suspect' joins the fodder

explanation.surface: People beginning to suspect that gender is a fluid thing rather than a fixed one.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird nests low in wet sedge meadows, which is where its name comes from. A topical-sounding opening word is the shuffle instruction, and the comma after 'we' hides where the fodder stops.
explanation.definitionFit: The sedge wren is a small bird that lives and breeds in wet sedge meadows, so 'marsh bird' places it by habitat.

clue.text: Inadequate to examine terms in theology

parts.note: to scan something is to examine it

indicators.note: a term is a boundary or limit, from the Latin terminus, so the letters wanted are the two at the ends

parts.note: the outer letters of the word, one from each end

explanation.surface: An examiner finding a divinity student's grasp of the vocabulary not good enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terms' is the trap: it reads as the technical vocabulary of a subject, and it is asking for the two ends of the word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Scanty means barely enough to do the job, which is what calling a supply inadequate says of it.

clue.text: On return, intend individual to receive college commendations

indicators.note: something on its return is travelling back the way it came, so these letters are read the other way round
a word that receives something opens up to hold it

parts.note: to aim at something is to intend it
an individual is a single one
c = college, as in the letters after a school's name

explanation.surface: A plan for one student to collect the college's praise when they get back.
explanation.walkthrough: Assemble the three pieces in the order the clue gives them, then read the whole lot backwards. Encomia is the plural of encomium, a formal speech in praise of somebody.
explanation.definitionFit: Encomia are formal speeches or writings in praise of a person, which is commendations at their most ceremonial.

clue.text: Manage certain farm output in Cheshire town

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
corn is one particular thing a farm produces, left unnamed by the clue

explanation.surface: Somebody managing a particular crop on land in Cheshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Runcorn is an industrial town on the Mersey in the north-west of England, and nothing in the surface admits that the answer is a place at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Runcorn is a town in Cheshire, so the definition names it by the county it stands in.

clue.text: Fix group of ships heading in opposite direction

indicators.note: a heading is both the letter at the front of a word and the compass course a vessel is steering
the course is turned through half the compass, so the letter standing for it is swapped for the one facing the other way

parts.note: ships are counted in sail, as in a fleet of twenty sail
the heading of those four letters is S for south, and the opposite point of the compass is N

explanation.surface: A fleet putting about and steaming back the way it came.
explanation.walkthrough: Everything turns on 'heading' meaning two things at once, and on S and N being compass points as well as letters. SAIL for a body of ships is the old naval count.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail something is to fasten it down, which is the fixing sense of 'fix' rather than the mending one.

clue.text: Awkward character during dinner-date?

indicators.note: during means inside the span of something, which is where these letters are sitting

parts.note: four consecutive letters of the hyphenated phrase, running straight across the hyphen

explanation.surface: A socially hopeless guest turning up in the middle of somebody's dinner date.
explanation.walkthrough: Solvers read straight over punctuation, so a hidden answer straddling a hyphen is the hardest sort to see. 'Character' is a person here, not a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A nerd is the socially clumsy, over-absorbed type, which is what 'awkward character' describes.

clue.text: A bit reminiscent, possibly, of senior politician

indicators.note: possibly says these letters could come out as something other than what they spell, so they are not in their settled order

parts.note: anagram fodder, fifteen letters

explanation.surface: Something that stirs a faint memory of somebody you have met before.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is the whole first half of the clue, which is what makes a fifteen-letter anagram hard to spot: count the letters against the enumeration before hunting for pieces. A Cabinet minister sits in the top tier of the British government.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cabinet minister runs a government department and sits in Cabinet, so 'senior politician' places them by rank.
